Now the Senator's office wants me prosecuted. | | [](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0ZZv_2TDjzvqsIVCD_4H6L8VJtyYJ_8e8Q82KWEKA4SCmpCnhcmtPIk9SatUFuLn1h5pwcSODPVll391IQGUkjKEEpZqk8A7j97g)
---
| NEW INVESTIGATION * ALASKA
---
THE BIG
MURKOWSKI
Anchorage. Primary day. No ID required.
This investigation cost **$50,000**. [Help us fund the next one.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0aqWeXeXJ0EUEgt2Ji_Xbyejf0lVDdsPejg7WpSc11Of8eXuen7E43Xmx88dAFEl7dzAjcXZEd-4cvjoGGvtoKeWsM_FcusKOxdA)
Dear Patriot,
Stand at that table with me for a second. Anchorage, Alaska. Primary day. There is a folding table, a laminated binder, and a perfectly nice woman working the poll book the way she probably has for years. I give her a name. It is not my name. The name is **Brian Murkowski**. He is the brother of a sitting United States Senator. He does not live in Alaska. He lives in Texas.
[ ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0buk1iL0HIKYBYCw3qav183JwKHMXSgvPQviDTXVj7pBsT9Gj5RcFSFMFGE_hY-tcSla41x-hz-cI38Y62Go7Tg1_az17t5JuBdg)
Then I tell her the one thing that is supposed to stop all of this cold. I tell her **I do not have my ID.** She looks up at me and says:
| "Absolutely possible."
---
ANCHORAGE POLL WORKER * AUGUST 18, 2026
I want you to watch this one for yourself. And then I want you to help me pay for the next one. **[You can chip in right here.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0cn0IdzgXpLG_Idq0UtVgOqDcHKxvnWaGoii_3P9gqD-gMAa1huuO3Z5VZciLk0OZagRVKH7FUAOCax28oFzZgarqFFWlcfHSKSw)** I asked her again anyway, because I wanted it recorded and I wanted it to be completely unmistakable to anyone who watched it later. All I have to do is fill out the question ballot, and then I can vote? **" Yes, sir."** We titled the video **" The Big Murkowski,"** and you really do have to laugh a little bit at it, because the only other available option is putting your head through a wall.
The funny part ends fast. **Every single thing I am about to tell you makes the thing before it worse.**
| ONE. A total stranger walked in off the street carrying no identification of any kind and was offered a ballot. TWO. The name on that ballot belongs to a United States Senator's brother who lives roughly three thousand miles away, in another state entirely. THREE. We did it again. Different polling place, same morning. One of my reporters gave the name **Karina Waller** -- Senator Murkowski's own **State Director**. No ID. Same offer. **[Help us keep doing exactly this.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0dXuldaI7n--wf39LC2KRYdLkhMYGpMujVAmM_I11XZcIGc4Z8x2LDP3yDGTgP42-rsMtKggQSFxXpXNPG--G_vy1JaeT_j9dFfA)** FOUR. Alaska law says you show identification to get a ballot, and the one narrow exception written into it is that the poll worker personally knows the person standing in front of them. Nobody in either of those buildings had ever laid eyes on us before in their lives. FIVE. Nobody wrote anything down. Nobody picked up a phone. Nobody flagged a single thing. We asked, we got our answer, and we walked back out the door.
---
Now here is the part that should stop you cold. Senator Murkowski has spent this year fighting the SAVE Act, which her office describes as "an overly burdensome, one-size-fits-all mandate from Washington," and the argument underneath that position has always been the same one we hear everywhere: that the hole we keep describing does not actually exist outside of our imagination. **We just showed her the hole. In her own state. Using her own brother's name.** Before anyone calls this a partisan hit job, let me say it plainly: Senator Murkowski is a Republican, and it does not matter to me even a little, because a hole in the process is a hole in the process and it does not care one bit about which party happens to walk through it. Her office did not say they were going to fix it. Her office said this:
| "Voter impersonation is a crime and should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law." OFFICE OF SEN. LISA MURKOWSKI
---
Now I want to be precise with you about what we did and did not do, because you fund this operation and you deserve that kind of accounting from me. **I did not vote. I did not sign anyone's name. I never touched a ballot.** I asked a question, I recorded the answer, and I left. That is what reporters do. The response from a sitting United States Senator's office was to start talking about prosecuting me for it. Patriot, this has become a pattern, and I want you to see it as clearly as I have come to see it over the last three weeks. Last week the Secretary of State of Minnesota published a statement accusing my journalists of **" lying, lawbreaking, and disruptions"** and announced that **law enforcement is reviewing** them. He never named a single law we broke. This week the office of a United States Senator is talking about prosecuting a journalist to the fullest extent of the law. Michigan. Minnesota. Alaska. Three states in three weeks, and every single time we have gone looking, we have found the same hole sitting there in plain sight. Nobody ever rushes to close the hole. **They come after the person holding the flashlight.**
[GIVE NOW -- FUND THE NEXT STATE](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0eONvzYuohzjn_t4iu_OpR0JbW_KtODU1i5wahEdzJCa0FSGy_8A37oYVd4Zplpl-GIk7oyGT1wwC37Ev9ArboaMnkaxy8qu0EnA)
Let me tell you what Alaska cost.
| $50,000
---
What this single investigation cost to produce -- so that you could hear two words said out loud at a folding table in Anchorage.
That covered the flights to Anchorage and back, the weeks of preparation before anyone ever got on a plane, the records work, the equipment, and a team standing on the ground at dawn on primary day three thousand miles from our office. It also covered the lawyers who reviewed every frame of that footage before a single second of it went to air, because we understood exactly what was coming the moment it did. I would spend every dollar of it again tomorrow morning without blinking. Here is my problem. **[We do not have another fifty thousand dollars sitting in a drawer waiting for the next state.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0fOCqhPa6FjjUpfzoYdQF8Y5KHK-WcgcY_QpjF63Bgb2JRNwwU40kGZkLXTzAtqG3u1e22ugyQNLprEwGBspoRTTIbfX5XqhgjDA)** And there is a next one. There is always a next one. Alaska is not special. Alaska is simply the state we happened to be standing in on Tuesday, and everything you are about to watch came out of a single morning and one honest question asked out loud at a folding table. **Imagine what is sitting untouched in the other forty-nine.** **In twenty-eight days, the first federal ballots for November go out.** After that date the machine is running, and everything we have not found yet gets voted on anyway. You and your family have to live under whatever comes out of those buildings, and so does mine, and that is the entire reason I keep walking into them with a camera when it would be far easier and considerably safer not to. There is nobody else writing this check, and there never has been. It has always been you.
[YES, JAMES -- I'LL HELP FUND THE NEXT ONE](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0g_TWtvoG2NPyT-Cb6qJ8mX6CIzvORrLMup9JYSUH-WV_maJaxWQUa87cpmX5TO_vFOT2djSskuUIHu_FwjZamqdAkxmWkRHh4Iw)
Thank you for everything you do. In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group
**P.S.** The video is called **" The Big Murkowski,"** and I hope it makes you laugh. Then I hope it makes you furious. A stranger with no ID was offered a United States Senator's brother's ballot, and the Senator's office answered by talking about prosecuting the man who filmed it. **[That is exactly why this cannot stop-- and you are the only reason it does not have to.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0hNDCfS_HGpWNL2K8ZXgKcwE9Vg0P8Fh1vtFzee2qXMB0hiFTPOx_J6jUe-y5wNLF2H7g2uyW-tZ_l_ClijKDRSMHd2MtIlQf7pA)**
[RUSH YOUR GIFT NOW](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AAwAAAAAAqUgbB0iXnomi2K9cxDLsl5VuDjTjXRcRX-k-rjBLl1UlsOg4ILTLEqSAyNN9H8biorXt8MyGrpgBi1Y0IvEynK0N2w0IASODTROF5EVAw)

We just showed her the hole. In her own state. Using her own brother's name. Before anyone calls this a partisan hit job, let me say it plainly: Senator Murkowski is a Republican, and it does not matter to me even a little, because a hole in the process is a hole in the process and it does not care one bit about which party happens to walk through it. Her office did not say they were going to fix it. Her office said this: | "Voter impersonation is a crime and should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law." OFFICE OF SEN. LISA MURKOWSKI Now I want to be precise with you about what we did and did not do, because you fund this operation and you deserve that kind of accounting from me. I did not vote. I did not sign anyone's name. I never touched a ballot. I asked a question, I recorded the answer, and I left. That is what reporters do. The response from a sitting United States Senator's office was to start talking about prosecuting me for it. Patriot, this has become a pattern, and I want you to see it as clearly as I have come to see it over the last three weeks. Last week the Secretary of State of Minnesota published a statement accusing my journalists of " lying, lawbreaking, and disruptions" and announced that law enforcement is reviewing them. He never named a single law we broke. This week the office of a United States Senator is talking about prosecuting a journalist to the fullest extent of the law. Michigan. Minnesota. Alaska. Three states in three weeks, and every single time we have gone looking, we have found the same hole sitting there in plain sight. Nobody ever rushes to close the hole. They come after the person holding the flashlight. Let me tell you what Alaska cost. | $50,000 What this single investigation cost to produce -- so that you could hear two words said out loud at a folding table in Anchorage. That covered the flights to Anchorage and back, the weeks of preparation before anyone ever got on a plane, the records work, the equipment, and a team standing on the ground at dawn on primary day three thousand miles from our office. It also covered the lawyers who reviewed every frame of that footage before a single second of it went to air, because we understood exactly what was coming the moment it did. I would spend every dollar of it again tomorrow morning without blinking. Here is my problem. And there is a next one. There is always a next one. Alaska is not special. Alaska is simply the state we happened to be standing in on Tuesday, and everything you are about to watch came out of a single morning and one honest question asked out loud at a folding table. Imagine what is sitting untouched in the other forty-nine. In twenty-eight days, the first federal ballots for November go out. After that date the machine is running, and everything we have not found yet gets voted on anyway. You and your family have to live under whatever comes out of those buildings, and so does mine, and that is the entire reason I keep walking into them with a camera when it would be far easier and considerably safer not to. There is nobody else writing this check, and there never has been. It has always been you. Thank you for everything you do. In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group P.S. The video is called " The Big Murkowski," and I hope it makes you laugh. Then I hope it makes you furious. A stranger with no ID was offered a United States Senator's brother's ballot, and the Senator's office answered by talking about prosecuting the man who filmed it. |

# [Even When We Disagree](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=213294303&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjEzMjk0MzAzLCJpYXQiOjE3ODgwMjQzODIsImV4cCI6MTc5MDYxNjM4MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.Cz0c_x4yU63OW2NWBxIDw9yA93b4Kd3vQn8UsPHbqyA)

---

On April 18, I walked onto the stage at the Michigan Democratic Party Convention as a candidate for the United States Senate and a four-term Democratic member of Congress.
I wasn't alone.
Behind me were volunteers, friends, supporters, and a notably healthy contingent from UNITE HERE Local 24--people who had knocked doors, made calls, organized workers, and given up their Saturday because they believed in what we were building.
Then they called my name.
And the room erupted.
Not in applause.
In boos.
They were loud enough that if you were standing in the convention hall--or watching the video later on your phone--you could barely hear a word I said.
Good freakin' grief.
What on earth had I done?
I hadn't abandoned the Democratic Party. I hadn't blocked voting rights or reproductive freedom. I hadn't spent my time in Washington manufacturing disagreements with Democratic leadership so I could get booked on cable television to talk about them.
Quite the opposite.
I've campaigned for every Democratic presidential nominee since I was old enough to vote. I worked for the party while I was still in college. I won a congressional district Donald Trump carried and then kept winning it. I helped elect other Democrats. I wrote legislation. I passed legislation. I showed up.
I was, by almost any conventional definition, a Democrat.
And my own Democratic convention was booing me off the stage.
Now, luckily, I'd been booed before.
Spend a few terms as a Democrat representing a district that voted for Donald Trump and you develop a certain tolerance for people yelling while you're holding a microphone.
But this was different.
These weren't MAGA protesters.
These were Democrats.
And this time, my supporters were standing up there with me.
My mother was standing up there with me.
Something in me switched on.
Maybe it was experience. Maybe stubbornness. Probably both.
But I wasn't going to stand frozen behind the podium waiting for the room to settle down.
So I walked.
I crossed the stage. I kept talking even though I could barely hear myself. I put my arm around the man next to me, lifted the microphone and called out over the noise:
"Democrats, even when we disagree, I love you."
A few months later, the morning after I lost the Democratic primary for the United States Senate by about a percentage point, I stood in front of Democrats again.
I started with the same words.
"Democrats, I love you even when we disagree."
I meant them both times.
But I've thought a lot since April about that last word.
Disagree.
Because disagreement wasn't really what I saw in that convention hall.
There were boos, yes.
There were also people screaming "F*** you, Haley Stevens."
There were people screaming "Zionist pig."
And suddenly a disagreement over one of the most painful, complicated conflicts on earth had become something much simpler: a verdict on whether someone belonged in the room at all.
That bothered me then.
It bothers me more now.
Not because my position on Israel is particularly mysterious. It isn't. I believe Israel has a right to exist and Israelis have a right to live in safety. I believe Palestinians deserve dignity, freedom and a state of their own. I believe this war has brought an unbearable amount of suffering. I have disagreed sharply with decisions made by the Netanyahu government. I want a permanent peace, and I believe the only durable path to one is two states.
You can disagree with any part of that.
That's politics.
But somewhere along the way, parts of our politics have begun confusing disagreement with disqualification.
That's something else.
After the convention, people came up to me and told me they were horrified. Some said they would never attend another party convention. Women of different ages and backgrounds have stopped me with tears in their eyes to say they were proud I stood my ground and heartbroken by what they watched happen.
Lordy lord.
My primary opponent, Abdul El-Sayed, reached out afterward. He spoke publicly, too. He didn't excuse what happened. He said it was wrong and asked people to be better.
That mattered to me.
Abdul is now Michigan's Democratic nominee for the United States Senate. He didn't create that moment, and I don't believe he wanted it.
I lost to him.
That's democracy, too.
And this isn't an essay about why I was right and everybody else was wrong. I'm not looking to be the hero of April 18. I'm certainly not interested in being its victim.
I ran because I believe things.
I still do.
I'm a manufacturing geek. Happily.
Before Congress, I worked on the Obama administration's auto rescue as chief of staff to Ron Bloom and Steve Rattner. I've spent my time in Congress working to strengthen American manufacturing, grow Michigan's innovation economy, support organized labor and make sure the country that invented modern manufacturing doesn't decide it's easier to buy everything from somewhere else.
I've visited hundreds of small businesses.
I've walked factory floors.
I've sat with workers worried about whether the plant will still be there when their kids are old enough to need a job.
Those experiences have shaped my politics at least as much as anything that happens inside the Capitol.
So has representing a district with a large and vibrant Jewish community.
So has serving as co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Hostage Task Force and helping lead the House to pass, 414-0, a resolution condemning Hamas and calling for the hostages to be released.
Four hundred and fourteen to zero.
And still Hersh Goldberg-Polin, an American citizen, was murdered after nearly eleven months in captivity.
None of this has given me simpler answers.
If anything, it has made me more suspicious of people who claim to have them.
Because the Middle East is not the source of every American grievance. It is not a shortcut for understanding every injustice. And no conflict--no matter how passionately we feel about it--should become permission to decide that everyone who sees it differently is corrupt, hateful or unwelcome.
There was another moment after the convention that stuck with me.
A popular local influencer reposted the video of me being booed and announced, essentially, that nobody liked me and I should drop out of the race.
Well.
I didn't.
I ran the race.
I lost it.
And now many of the same people who spent the primary demanding ideological purity are confronting uncomfortable questions of their own about rhetoric, antisemitism and where criticism ends and something uglier begins.
There is a lesson in that, although probably not the one anybody wants to hear.
Political coalitions are easy when everybody agrees.
They're also unnecessary.
The whole purpose of a coalition is to hold people together who don't.
Michigan Democrats will gather again this weekend. This time, the primary is over. We have our nominees. November is about 65 days away.
There will be disagreements.
Good.
There should be.
Democracy isn't supposed to make disagreement disappear. It's supposed to give us a way to live with it.
Voting is personal and private. Political engagement is loud and public and frequently inconvenient. Democracy is messy because human beings are messy.
The alternative isn't a cleaner democracy.
It's less democracy.
April wasn't my moment.
Neither, ultimately, was this Senate race.
I wasn't warmly embraced at my own convention. I didn't win the nomination I spent more than a year fighting for.
And you know what?
I'm still here.
I'm still a Democrat.
I still believe science matters. I still believe health care should be affordable and accessible. I still believe working people deserve more power in an economy that has given too much of it away. I still believe organized labor built the middle class. I still believe women should control their own bodies and every eligible American should be able to cast a ballot without politicians putting obstacles in their way.
I still believe America should make things.
I still believe our alliances matter.
And I still believe the Democratic Party is big enough to contain people who disagree with one another.
It has to be.
Because elections happen. Somebody wins. Somebody loses. Governments form. Coalitions shift.
And then we do the whole ridiculous, extraordinary thing again.
Meanwhile, Americans wake up every morning with considerably more immediate problems.
The rent is due.
The grocery bill is too high.
The factory down the road is laying people off.
A parent can't afford a prescription.
A young couple can't afford a house.
A worker wants a union and is scared they'll lose their job for saying so.
Those problems aren't going to be solved by finding another Democrat to throw out of the room.
They're going to be solved by figuring out how to stay in the room together long enough to do something about them.
Even when we disagree.

A few months later, the morning after I lost the Democratic primary for the United States Senate by about a percentage point, I stood in front of Democrats again. I started with the same words. "Democrats, I love you even when we disagree." I meant them both times. But I've thought a lot since April about that last word. Disagree. Because disagreement wasn't really what I saw in that convention hall. There were boos, yes. There were also people screaming "F*** you, Haley Stevens." There were people screaming "Zionist pig." And suddenly a disagreement over one of the most painful, complicated conflicts on earth had become something much simpler: a verdict on whether someone belonged in the room at all. That bothered me then. It bothers me more now. Not because my position on Israel is particularly mysterious. It isn't. I believe Israel has a right to exist and Israelis have a right to live in safety. I believe Palestinians deserve dignity, freedom and a state of their own. I believe this war has brought an unbearable amount of suffering. I have disagreed sharply with decisions made by the Netanyahu government. I want a permanent peace, and I believe the only durable path to one is two states. You can disagree with any part of that. That's politics. But somewhere along the way, parts of our politics have begun confusing disagreement with disqualification. That's something else. After the convention, people came up to me and told me they were horrified. Some said they would never attend another party convention. Women of different ages and backgrounds have stopped me with tears in their eyes to say they were proud I stood my ground and heartbroken by what they watched happen. Lordy lord. My primary opponent, Abdul El-Sayed, reached out afterward. He spoke publicly, too. He didn't excuse what happened. He said it was wrong and asked people to be better. That mattered to me. Abdul is now Michigan's Democratic nominee for the United States Senate. He didn't create that moment, and I don't believe he wanted it. I lost to him. That's democracy, too. And this isn't an essay about why I was right and everybody else was wrong. I'm not looking to be the hero of April 18. I'm certainly not interested in being its victim. I ran because I believe things. I still do. I'm a manufacturing geek. Happily. Before Congress, I worked on the Obama administration's auto rescue as chief of staff to Ron Bloom and Steve Rattner. I've spent my time in Congress working to strengthen American manufacturing, grow Michigan's innovation economy, support organized labor and make sure the country that invented modern manufacturing doesn't decide it's easier to buy everything from somewhere else. I've visited hundreds of small businesses. I've walked factory floors. I've sat with workers worried about whether the plant will still be there when their kids are old enough to need a job. Those experiences have shaped my politics at least as much as anything that happens inside the Capitol. So has representing a district with a large and vibrant Jewish community. So has serving as co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Hostage Task Force and helping lead the House to pass, 414-0, a resolution condemning Hamas and calling for the hostages to be released. Four hundred and fourteen to zero. And still Hersh Goldberg-Polin, an American citizen, was murdered after nearly eleven months in captivity. None of this has given me simpler answers. If anything, it has made me more suspicious of people who claim to have them. Because the Middle East is not the source of every American grievance. It is not a shortcut for understanding every injustice. And no conflict--no matter how passionately we feel about it--should become permission to decide that everyone who sees it differently is corrupt, hateful or unwelcome. There was another moment after the convention that stuck with me. A popular local influencer reposted the video of me being booed and announced, essentially, that nobody liked me and I should drop out of the race. Well. I didn't. I ran the race. I lost it. And now many of the same people who spent the primary demanding ideological purity are confronting uncomfortable questions of their own about rhetoric, antisemitism and where criticism ends and something uglier begins. There is a lesson in that, although probably not the one anybody wants to hear. Political coalitions are easy when everybody agrees. They're also unnecessary. The whole purpose of a coalition is to hold people together who don't. Michigan Democrats will gather again this weekend. This time, the primary is over. We have our nominees. November is about 65 days away. There will be disagreements. Good. There should be. Democracy isn't supposed to make disagreement disappear. It's supposed to give us a way to live with it. Voting is personal and private. Political engagement is loud and public and frequently inconvenient. Democracy is messy because human beings are messy. The alternative isn't a cleaner democracy. It's less democracy. April wasn't my moment. Neither, ultimately, was this Senate race. I wasn't warmly embraced at my own convention. I didn't win the nomination I spent more than a year fighting for. And you know what? I'm still here. I'm still a Democrat. I still believe science matters. I still believe health care should be affordable and accessible. I still believe working people deserve more power in an economy that has given too much of it away. I still believe organized labor built the middle class. I still believe women should control their own bodies and every eligible American should be able to cast a ballot without politicians putting obstacles in their way. I still believe America should make things. I still believe our alliances matter. And I still believe the Democratic Party is big enough to contain people who disagree with one another. It has to be. Because elections happen. Somebody wins. Somebody loses. Governments form. Coalitions shift. And then we do the whole ridiculous, extraordinary thing again. Meanwhile, Americans wake up every morning with considerably more immediate problems. The rent is due. The grocery bill is too high. The factory down the road is laying people off. A parent can't afford a prescription. A young couple can't afford a house. A worker wants a union and is scared they'll lose their job for saying so. Those problems aren't going to be solved by finding another Democrat to throw out of the room. They're going to be solved by figuring out how to stay in the room together long enough to do something about them. Even when we disagree. **By Wendy Yurgo**
We would never knowingly hand an eight-year-old something engineered to make him crave the next hit, yet millions of parents do exactly that every day. We call it an iPad.
No, the hit is not a drug. It is the next level, the next win, the next Roblox reward, the next rare item, the next notification, the next surprise that may or may not appear when a child taps the screen. I am not interested in making hysterical comparisons the research does not support. I am interested in why so many children cannot seem to put these devices down, why taking them away can produce an astonishing reaction, and why we continue pretending the technology itself has nothing to do with it.
For years we called this "screen time," which made the whole thing sound relatively harmless. Too much television was screen time. A movie was screen time. Playing Pac-Man was screen time. What children are holding today is something altogether different. The screen is simply the delivery mechanism. Behind it sits technology designed to learn what keeps a user engaged, deliver rewards, introduce novelty, personalize the experience, and eliminate the natural stopping points that used to tell us it was time to go do something else.
That is what we are putting up against a developing child's brain.
And then we blame the child when the technology wins.
The American Academy of Pediatrics has finally moved the conversation beyond counting hours and toward examining what it calls the digital ecosystem surrounding children. It is about time. An hour spent FaceTiming Grandma is not the same thing as an hour spent inside a game engineered around rewards, advancement, social interaction, and repeated engagement. Content matters. Design matters. What the child is doing matters. Most of all, what the technology is doing to keep the child there matters.
Children are still developing impulse control, judgment, delayed gratification, and emotional regulation. That process takes years. The technology sitting across from them suffers from no such developmental disadvantage. It is backed by some of the most sophisticated companies on earth, extraordinary amounts of behavioral data, and a business model that benefits when the user stays longer, comes back sooner, and engages more.
That is not a fair fight.
## **Follow the Reward**
And then there is dopamine, the word everyone seems afraid to use.
Every win, rare item, advancement, sound, animation or unexpected reward can reinforce the desire to do it again. Drugs obviously act on the brain through very different biological mechanisms, and I am not equating an iPad with a street drug. But addiction researchers have spent decades studying reward, reinforcement, craving and impaired control. The technology industry understands those same human vulnerabilities remarkably well.
The reward does not even have to arrive every time. Unpredictability can make reinforcement more powerful because the user keeps trying to discover whether the next attempt will deliver it.
Any parent who has heard their child say, "Just three more minutes," only to hear the same thing three minutes later, knows exactly what I am talking about. What starts as a few more minutes turns into a negotiation and, too often, an argument when the device finally goes off. If you have ever physically taken an iPad out of a child's hands and watched the reaction, you already know this is not the same thing as telling him it is time to put away his Legos.
The AAP calls part of what is happening here variable reinforcement. Parents do not need the terminology. We have watched it play out in our own homes.
The AAP now expressly discusses problematic digital media use that can become excessive or compulsive and design features that prolong engagement. The American Psychiatric Association has gone further, identifying Internet Gaming Disorder as a condition warranting further study and describing behaviors that include preoccupation with gaming, withdrawal when gaming is removed, unsuccessful attempts to control participation, and continued excessive use despite problems.
Then there is the brain research. A systematic review of neuroimaging studies involving adolescents with gaming disorder found neurological changes the researchers described as comparable to those seen in substance addiction, including impairments involving emotional regulation, reward-seeking, inhibition and risky decision-making.
That does not make gaming cocaine, and it certainly does not make every child who plays a video game an addict. But it should end the ridiculous argument that parents concerned about the addictive nature of these products are simply being hysterical.
The next round, the rare reward, the absolute meltdown when the device is finally taken away. None of this is happening in a vacuum. The companies building these products understand reinforcement very well. Parents should too.

## **Now Add ADHD**
Now consider children who already struggle with attention, executive functioning or impulse control. Research has found an association between ADHD symptoms and gaming disorder. That does not mean gaming causes ADHD. It means a child already struggling to regulate attention and impulses may be especially vulnerable to a digital environment offering immediate stimulation and repeated reward.
I have watched it in my own children, and I finally reached the point where what I was seeing became impossible to ignore. The attachment to the devices was changing. Their behavior around them was changing. Their attitudes were changing. Getting off became a fight. Ordinary life was increasingly competing against something capable of producing instant entertainment every few seconds.
My kids even talk about "Brainrots" while playing Roblox. In one wildly popular experience on the Roblox platform, children chase collectible characters through a constant cycle of acquiring, earning and upgrading. Yes, they are actually called Brainrots. You cannot make this stuff up.
But Roblox is one platform. This is much bigger than Roblox.
We have built an entire childhood culture around eliminating boredom. A child gets restless at dinner, give him the iPad. Long car ride, iPad. Waiting room, iPad. Meltdown, find the iPad. Good behavior, reward her with the iPad.
And yes, I have done it too. What parent hasn't?
The problem is that boredom is not an emergency. Neither is waiting. Neither is frustration. Children are supposed to experience all three. They are supposed to figure out what to do when nothing interesting is happening. They are supposed to sit through conversations that do not revolve around them. They are supposed to lose games, wait their turn, read things that unfold slowly, and discover that the world does not produce a flashing reward every fifteen seconds.
Those experiences are not inconveniences standing in the way of childhood. They are childhood.
And I started wondering what we were teaching children when every uncomfortable emotion, empty minute or tedious experience could immediately be escaped through a device.
## **I Took Them Away**
Eventually I substantially restricted the devices in my own home.
I did not do it because I had just read a study. I did it because I know my children, and I did not like what I was watching.
Then I watched what happened without them.
My children became more present. They engaged more. The constant pull toward the device began to fade. Ordinary things became interesting again. I could see the difference.
That experience sent me deeper into the research, and what I found made me angry because parents have spent years being told that everything happening inside this digital ecosystem is ultimately our failure to manage it properly.
Set limits. Use parental controls. Watch them more closely. Take the device away.
Yes. Absolutely.
I have been writing about children's online safety for years, and parents have an enormous responsibility to know what their children are doing online. But parental responsibility does not absolve corporate responsibility.
That defense just collapsed under an $18 billion settlement.
On August 26, Meta agreed to pay up to $18 billion over ten years to resolve claims by nearly every state that Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict children. Meta denied wrongdoing. Florida refused to join the settlement, arguing that it did not go far enough. Still, Meta agreed to set two hours as the default daily limit for minors, block access from midnight to 6 a.m., mute notifications during school hours, and hide like counts.
Those are not content controls. They are brakes on the engagement machine. After years of telling parents to manage the product better, Meta has agreed to redesign the product itself.
Why should parents have to continually defend their children from products built for children?
If a toy company announced that its product observed what held a child's attention, refined the experience based upon that behavior, delivered rewards designed to increase interaction, and became more profitable the longer the child used it, parents would have questions. If that company then shrugged when children had difficulty disengaging and told us we should have imposed better limits, we would have even more.
Put the same business model behind a touchscreen and somehow we call it innovation.
## **Your Child 's Attention Is Worth Money**
A child's attention has economic value. That is the ugly truth underneath this entire conversation.
Platforms built around advertising, purchases, subscriptions or engagement have every reason to keep users engaged and coming back. The more they learn about what holds an individual child's attention, the better they can become at serving whatever is likely to hold it next.
Adults cannot resist this stuff. Look around any restaurant and count how many grown adults are staring at their phones.
Yet we expect a nine-year-old to demonstrate better impulse control.
That is absurd.
I am not calling for a ban on technology, and I am not pretending every video game is evil. Some games are creative. Technology can educate, connect and inspire. Our children are growing up in a digital world, and pretending otherwise is pointless.
The question is who controls whom.
We have spent years worrying about what children may encounter once they are online: pornography, predators, bullying, violence, exploitation, and the dark communities I have written about extensively. Those dangers are real. But there is a more basic question that comes first.
Why does the child keep going back?
We need to stop treating that question as an indictment of the child or the parent and start examining the machine sitting in the child's hands.
I have.
And I no longer care whether my children think taking it away is unfair.
An iPad is not childhood. Roblox is not a developmental necessity. Gaming is not a constitutional right. Sometimes being a parent means taking away the thing your child desperately wants.
And sometimes the desperation tells you everything you need to know.
**We are the parents. The machine belongs to us. The childhood belongs to them.**
**Turn it off.**

Still, Meta agreed to set two hours as the default daily limit for minors, block access from midnight to 6 a.m., mute notifications during school hours, and hide like counts. Those are not content controls. They are brakes on the engagement machine. After years of telling parents to manage the product better, Meta has agreed to redesign the product itself. Why should parents have to continually defend their children from products built for children? If a toy company announced that its product observed what held a child's attention, refined the experience based upon that behavior, delivered rewards designed to increase interaction, and became more profitable the longer the child used it, parents would have questions. If that company then shrugged when children had difficulty disengaging and told us we should have imposed better limits, we would have even more. Put the same business model behind a touchscreen and somehow we call it innovation. Your Child 's Attention Is Worth Money A child's attention has economic value. That is the ugly truth underneath this entire conversation. Platforms built around advertising, purchases, subscriptions or engagement have every reason to keep users engaged and coming back. The more they learn about what holds an individual child's attention, the better they can become at serving whatever is likely to hold it next. Adults cannot resist this stuff. Look around any restaurant and count how many grown adults are staring at their phones. Yet we expect a nine-year-old to demonstrate better impulse control. That is absurd. I am not calling for a ban on technology, and I am not pretending every video game is evil. Some games are creative. Technology can educate, connect and inspire. Our children are growing up in a digital world, and pretending otherwise is pointless. The question is who controls whom. We have spent years worrying about what children may encounter once they are online: pornography, predators, bullying, violence, exploitation, and the dark communities I have written about extensively. Those dangers are real. But there is a more basic question that comes first. Why does the child keep going back? We need to stop treating that question as an indictment of the child or the parent and start examining the machine sitting in the child's hands. I have. And I no longer care whether my children think taking it away is unfair. An iPad is not childhood. Roblox is not a developmental necessity. Gaming is not a constitutional right. Sometimes being a parent means taking away the thing your child desperately wants. And sometimes the desperation tells you everything you need to know. We are the parents. The machine belongs to us. The childhood belongs to them. Turn it off. About the Author Wendy M. Yurgo is a Christian, attorney, entrepreneur, and the Founder and CEO of Revere Payments, a conservative fintech company serving many of the nation's leading faith based and freedom driven organizations. She writes about where faith collides with the systems shaping our culture, bringing a legal and executive lens to the most urgent issues of our time. subject: Totally out of control
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate
body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=2779%2E5691347%2E-voT6-)

Peter,
First of all, I want to say thank you.
Let me explain why:
This campaign has raised an extraordinary amount of money from an extraordinary number of people giving small-dollar, grassroots donations. That grassroots support is something that I’m grateful for every day. I promise you, Peter: _I never, ever take you or your support for granted._
But the reality is that even with that unprecedented level of grassroots support, we still have critical fundraising goals to meet in the final stretch of this campaign to build the resources it’ll take to win here in Georgia.
The Senate GOP’s main Super PAC — which is just one of many right-wing Super PACs who could spend money on this race — has raised more than $500 million. And then there’s still Trump and his Super PAC, plus other far-right billionaires like Elon Musk waiting in the wings.
The truth is that MAGA can spend endlessly attacking us because they’ve got an army of billionaires and corporate PAC donors lining up to fund the smears.
_We expect to be outspent in this race,_ possibly by hundreds of millions of dollars. We don’t need to match the Super PACs dollar for dollar, but we do need to make sure we get our message out.
So please, I’m humbly asking:
[**Can you give $5 to my reelection campaign today to help me fight back against the dark money Super PACs who are going to flood Georgia with attacks? Donate today to fight their lies with the TRUTH >>>**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-aug26.Gm-cyv&refcode=em260829-2-subs&utm_campaign=em260829-2-subs&t=2&akid=2779%2E5691347%2E-voT6-)
_Post-Citizens United_ , Super PACs and secret money in politics are totally out of control, corrupting policymaking on behalf of the rich and powerful.
And when members of Congress aren't fundraising from lobbyists and corporate PACs, they're just trying to dodge getting bombed by these Super PACs.
Candidates all over the country are facing down hundreds of millions in Super PAC spending from dark-money groups that don’t even disclose their donors until after the election, if ever.
Is this the way we want our government to work? Do we really want to allow unlimited, secret political money to bend the nation’s agenda in darkness?
Peter: All across Georgia and all across the country, a wave is building. The kind of wave that comes once a generation, when the people have been pushed too far and decide all together, all at once: **enough is enough.**
That is the message that we’re going to send when we WIN this November.
Yes, this election will be tough.
But I know how to win tough fights. I’ve done it before.
Let’s do it again.
[**Please, consider making a donation to my reelection campaign today. I wouldn’t ask if it didn’t make a real difference, Peter.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-aug26.Gm-cyv&refcode=em260829-2-subs&utm_campaign=em260829-2-subs&t=3&akid=2779%2E5691347%2E-voT6-)
Thank you, sincerely, for chipping in if you can and for everything you do to support this campaign and this movement.
As always,
Jon

**Yes. It is the same thumbnail.**
Look, we all look extremely good in that picture. David looks distinguished, Hunter looks like a man who has made peace with a few things, and I look like someone who was told there would be tequila. Why mess with perfection.
_**Here is why I am sending you another Hunter Biden email anyway.**_
When he sat down with David Shuster and me, we got to a subject most interviewers steer around, and most guests are grateful to have steered around. It was pointed out to him--directly, on camera--that some of the rhetoric circulating right now edges up against an old antisemitic trope about Jews and money.
He did not deflect. He said it has been a problem for him. He said he gets accused of giving safe harbor to antisemitism by one crowd and called "the son of the genocide Joe" by another, and that there is no winning that.
And then he did something I have watched exactly no one else do on a political show this year. He gave a history lesson.

"Where is our Micah today?" he asked. "Where is our Jeremiah to stand up to Solomon and say: you are him."

Peter, I went back and forth on if I should send you this or not. Not because I didn't know what to say, but because I knew how much it would hurt to say it. It’s difficult to admit that I can't do this alone. [**There's so much weighing on me right now, and finding the right words feels impossible. Working cows and driving tractors growing up made me who I am today. It taught me the value of hard work, the importance of keeping your word, and what it means to sacrifice for something bigger than yourself. Trust me, I know all the constant emails and texts can weigh on you. It wears on me too. Some days I wonder if it's worth it. But then I remember why I'm here. I didn't come to Washington because I love asking true patriots like you for money. I didn't run for Congress at 29 years old to become the youngest House Republican so I could spend my nights begging for donations. I came because my kids deserve to grow up in a better America than I grew up in — and right now, that's not guaranteed. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids, I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They're everything to me. They're the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I've committed my life and career to. And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father Almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. I refuse to look my kids in the eye someday and tell them I gave up when it mattered most. [**That's why I'm still here. That's why I keep sending these messages.**](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/f-mmn5VtuL3SvR8FqMvdZfAJtvCtExMH9dyOzm1fjEWClVw49ss_iEGL81KY69jmFUO5ue75p1mIzEnCcYQ_xpiqk_3RakAfDKp4XTryPMWyG4i2IW_rnFcrpnjQt-f86cnEVOViniaJuf6F-zlEKsdlft-eEH0cbkjr4ALzal0drOyhMD6uu-zkR4P3lfRA41kQQcNsAxpd8i0DBaLO2e1geECogLhV1o4eZQgPfWcMlxvqVYkrMW-ukUAmKcUxlcVh0dMqKKCGDGrkCxWcnSXQVb_jfQ2CUqhM3MEVbcjU-QhEJPg7RDGREcalxFsxvR-AxrDQb_uOmLoMQFMcNlgX7gZceUdMGeG4Z6tfLWX2j6aB-nWmTNJi04XquYaY8mslgXJ0NBtj3bArhGgVWHubGdM2f3FMhjheK5am7QxMF4O6RTJiClu_HU9UfyG2xeYp6o5gU5GRBRTzGdM4rNX4iF6uH3jQEdQqve5upATC2UXP0Koc7jd7x2A-BzLhLj4_IQqpzPkcG5plOAOOJa1IN1rw0B96dq-AWALTmVVcjf2ZK8mjuwcwkV_aZBlBnbNcVrfG4weiGqVwPpXyIrZB7mcROosdF017hP9-zDEE7XKjJWP3_FHL7_5S41fWvDEbKmfkZwhAKETqTN_zOjBq6NjKhYxIcbWm94Lkve4ILinOk-7k4AjgP85bh-IRmnwyr36csgh-B4sIhRFbnrT4U52VYfE8StvzU20fZDjit2aqmIILybNCOXPu-FApJwtW72T616l0vPZGyzJFjP39ZBDPiaP_9gtLv3RwLoqPgf4/CwlMAydvVayDWJJXKyI7146AwHQiZ_td/24) Because nothing — I repeat — nothing is more important to me than fighting off the vicious leftist attacks against the soul of our country. The left hates you. They hate your vote. They hate MAGA for putting America First. And they will do anything — lie, cheat, steal, destroy — to ensure your children inherit a country you won't even recognize. Peter, today I'll make the same promise to you that I've made to myself, to my wife, and to my children: As long as I live, I will continue to FIGHT to preserve the soul of our country. No force on Earth will push me to abandon my mission and calling. Not the attacks. Not the exhaustion. Not the constant pressure to give up and go home. Believe me, I'm not someone who finds it easy to ask for support. Texting and emailing you like this is the last thing I thought I'd have to do when I ran for Congress. But the country we love is on the brink of destruction, and God has put it on my heart to fight with all that I have — even when that means swallowing my pride and asking for help. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

_Repeatedly lying under oath. Replacing world-class experts with quacks. Sowing doubt in proven-effective vaccines. Censoring studies that don’t support his delusions. subject: Tell DHS to stop spying on our communities
body:
They tracked license plates, monitored chats, and infiltrated lawful meetings | |
---
Peter, **The Department of Homeland Security called it**** _“Operation Puppet Master.”_****Federal agents in Minnesota infiltrated meetings in churches, union halls, libraries, parks, and schools while surveilling people organizing against Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown.** Agents monitored activist chats, collected license plate numbers, used facial recognition, and obtained years of financial records from unions and advocacy groups. One DHS presentation even placed 18 organizations on a slide labeled “The Conspiracy.” That is designed to intimidate people out of organizing. No one should have to wonder whether joining a protest, attending a union meeting, or gathering with their neighbors will put them in a federal surveillance file. **At OnePA, we know our power comes from people organizing together. We cannot allow DHS to treat constitutionally protected organizing and speech as grounds for suspicion.** [**Tell Congress to investigate “Operation Puppet Master” and stop DHS from surveilling churches, unions, activists, and communities exercising their rights.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38KVdNnkS7loVZEkhB07L__71O0imNKJq8LfXCjnNV5oI7XmExJLU1qO5ue3XD0Vkbbc2VNFZDf_O-nU6zOfQL7igKTrk14jgt_WVX43pHXp3gfNT4WgNN3kv6sugojUG79Y5QfWOg9_LuVhXSIPQ__PkVqvptGrqCGIKChJBgwvgOhtTcBLV-aZQvJHqcikp8EnCVCxNSquWwNAX_Ts7jz7G1flfakVVIzMy3dyQJj-8fd-VugHBbOnqN3uediUOPNaP_yc4FhjRWC5omFue7aaj8qy8awjSEKGG5zOWy1esagY97As7WEFcPwcnQeXXzAgCL2bTSGHmmRm4AFNJsvBt7L7b0dDtfJNeklNMN7g18d_P_RcW5qZ9PtfV8_e_8sYpzBL27NNVerRYjELcrRQZkxGeLLXO_ydneaDuAsGpTJiIS6NQB0XDw9lTQD567oRHJYi15iVaSuDxu0DVss/4tl/CBmB8QN_Qzili3mK6z8iyw/h0/h001.KuiGe-qT9dBWTXzY3gzs25ugXgugfouUpGaIrMpleTQ) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38KVdNnkS7loVZEkhB07L__71O0imNKJq8LfXCjnNV5oI7XmExJLU1qO5ue3XD0Vkbbc2VNFZDf_O-nU6zOfQL7igKTrk14jgt_WVX43pHXp3gfNT4WgNN3kv6sugojUG79Y5QfWOg9_LuVhXSIPQ__PkVqvptGrqCGIKChJBgwvgOhtTcBLV-aZQvJHqcikp8EnCVCxNSquWwNAX_Ts7jz7G1flfakVVIzMy3dyQJj-7MVRyJI7MQ7yVzKRZUrpXu7nmKcat9hXV5rDaoUd9gkPAO0sLGU_Sx6Yrt6FlNLAEnZoAIlxJzW_7bgw2Cf4o2dIf2BP9uZn5WFL0cr5R5wJ1yoh0OblXGmF9dRxIdPvPoAJ7_iCk11oZt1suKn3LHDZJVFmKMIaviad1a22T1WeXodYeOQunCDXUnGtUAPmUeuEClKbuIxn2mvj7DQiDjHwr2wy6Gq5pz6NDwBvOrf/4tl/CBmB8QN_Qzili3mK6z8iyw/h1/h001.m_lqmrR7tL4bG05DNlVTciyteaMXd5pKZh4M0_-aZJk)

**This threat reaches far beyond Minnesota. The same tools can be turned against workers organizing unions, tenants demanding better housing, Black communities building political power, or anyone challenging this administration’s illegal policies.**
Former DHS Sec. Kristi Noem was widely regarded as one of the most lawless, corrupt, and reckless DHS secretaries in modern history. And her replacement, Markwayne Mullin, is an open election denier.
Our rights to speak, assemble, worship, organize, and protest cannot depend on whether the Trump administration approves of what we are saying.
OnePA’s work is rooted in building the kind of lasting community power that no administration can simply switch off. That means creating spaces where neighbors can come together, develop leaders, and act collectively without being watched, tracked, or treated like a threat for demanding a voice in the decisions that shape their lives.
**People organizing together have always changed this country. We will not let government surveillance scare our communities into silence.**

body:
Blocking a GOP supermajority in North Carolina.
#
Hi there,
In 2024, North Carolina voters elected Democratic Governor Josh Stein and successfully broke the Republicans' veto-proof supermajority in the State House.
**In 2026, our goal is to keep it that way.**
Holding key State House and State Senate seats will ensure the governor's veto remains a meaningful check on legislative power, preventing one-party rule in a swing state that will play a pivotal role in the 2028 presidential election.
And in addition to the veto, there’s another reason legislative seats are so important in North Carolina. Under the state constitution, the governor has no veto power over redistricting maps—a fact that Republicans in the North Carolina legislature have taken full advantage of in recent years.
Pushed by Trump’s gerrymandering spree in multiple red states across the country, the General Assembly recently enacted an aggressive mid-decade gerrymander, scrambling competitive districts like North Carolina’s 1st Congressional District and altering county lines to secure an unfair partisan advantage.
When Republicans hold unchecked supermajorities, they can bypass Governor Stein entirely, overriding vetoes on voting access, reproductive freedom, public school funding, and emergency relief programs. Protecting state legislative seats is our most critical line of defense against total legislative overreach.
**That’s why our strategy in North Carolina includes defending key State House seats to block a Republican supermajority and protect Governor Stein’s veto power, and flipping targeted seats to break the Republican supermajority in the State Senate.**
By funding state legislative caucuses and fueling voter contact right now, we can protect the Governor’s veto and limit North Carolina Republicans’ power to further redraw maps in their favor.
[**Will you make a donation to the North Carolina Win in the States Fund today to block a supermajority in the State House, break a supermajority in the State Senate, and protect Governor Stein’s veto?**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-nc-2026.u25aHV&refcode=em20260829-2612&t=1&akid=2612%2E1562180%2EfGSbGs)
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-nc-2026.u25aHV&refcode=em20260829-2612&t=2&akid=2612%2E1562180%2EfGSbGs)**
Thank you for being part of this work.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260829-2&t=3&refcode2=2612_1562180_fGSbGs&akid=2612%2E1562180%2EfGSbGs)

body:
| Friend, it's Mary Trump.

Five years ago, after the attack on the Capitol, I said my uncle was unstable and needed to be removed from office immediately.

**_I was right then, and the case is only more clear now._**

I've made this argument as a clinical psychologist, as his niece, and as someone who grew up watching exactly how my family wields power. My opinion as to whether Donald is capable of doing the job of the presidency has never wavered, and the evidence should be even more obvious to anyone willing to look.

Consider what we've all watched recently. Donald calls foreign leaders by the wrong names. He invents countries that don't exist. He cannot stay awake through his own meetings. His hands are bruised, his ankles are swollen, and he has no impulse control. [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/127403?t=6&akid=28306%2E878179%2EtKl3Na) **Here's the part I most need you to understand: Donald isn't a different person. His cognitive, psychological, and physical decline are simply revealing who he's always been.**

Meanwhile, the people constitutionally empowered to act — his Cabinet, his party — are painfully aware of his unfitness even as they work to cover it up. They have decided that their own hold on power is worth more to them than the country's safety or the rights of the people they purport to serve. They will not act on their own.

**So the responsibility falls to us, and the only real remedy available to us is an electoral one. We are less than three months from Election Day, and what we build between now and then will determine whether this man spends his final two years in office with a Congress that indulges him or one that finally holds him to account.**

That is what Transcend PAC exists to fund. We back candidates who can flip the House, invest in the Senate races that get us to a majority, and put real money into the state races almost nobody is watching.

| | _Mark Warner here. My friend Tom Perriello is running for Congress to flip Virginia’s Fifth District, and I wanted to make sure you saw his message below:_ It’s official – the path back to national sanity runs through our district, Virginia's Fighting Fifth!

**That’s right, the DCCC has just elevated our race to the coveted Red to Blue status, given to the highest tier of pick-up opportunities needed to reclaim a Democratic majority.**

This has been a huge week of momentum, starting with a new poll that shows our months of barnstorming the district have paid off – we have pulled even with Rep. John McGuire in a district he won by 15 points less than two years ago. Better yet, when voters hear about his record, we pull away by ten points. That’s what happens when he sells out our communities to protect his 100% rating from the corporate lobbyists in DC.

[_**If you love this momentum as much as I do, don’t bother reading the rest of this email. Just click here to split a donation between my campaign and Mark Warner so we can reach the voters who will do the rest. Let’s leave nothing on the table to ensure we reclaim this seat for the people of the Fighting Fifth.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138159861/643222022/814158331?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_Perriello_260829_T1_2&refcode2=260829_em_markwarner&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2Y2M5ZGMwNy1lMGEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eysRQ6BPQ59z8oGeCWUoWanyrZLdguQnRavNanPmvDA=)

The DCCC’s Red to Blue program is a highly competitive group of top-tier races across the country. Getting added to this list sends a big signal that this is the place to invest your time, talent, and treasure, if you want to reclaim our country from the kleptocrat-in-chief.

The path back to sanity runs through the Virginia Fifth and the defeat of John McGuire. He was part of January 6th, has been enriching himself day trading stocks, and is so extreme that he opposes a right to contraception. He has been AWOL from the district, while voting to shutter rural health clinics and labor and delivery units. He got caught insider trading stocks in companies impacted by his party’s work in Congress.

This news shows that a campaign like ours – one that rejects money from lobbyists and focuses on grassroots energy – can get the resources we need to flip this seat.

I’m proud that our grassroots campaign has already defied the odds. But being a Red to Blue race isn’t all sunshine and puppies – it also means that the Republicans’ dark money juggernaut will be unleashing on us soon. Big time.

They see the same numbers we see, and the dark money groups know that one of their most reliable yes men, John McGuire, is in trouble. BIG trouble. The President can’t save him, because the voters here have turned on Trump. Every one of those "endorsed by Trump” posters McGuire has planted around the district is just driving his numbers down further.

All that’s left is McGuire’s undying loyalty to his dark money donors. He sold out our communities for them, and they are going to spend a lot to protect him.

And that opponent, of course, is yours truly. He’s not talking about property taxes, or the minimum wage, or the $24 billion budget surplus he and Greg Abbott have spent on border stunts and data center tax breaks instead of the people of Texas. _**Houston is not the only city to notice...**_

The **San Antonio Express-News** ran an op-ed this week asking a simple question: Dan Patrick, why won't you debate Vikki Goodwin?
The piece laid out the mess of Patrick’s “legacy” in Texas politics: the campaign donations he took from Elon Musk while handing $1 BILLION in tax incentives to data centers last year alone. Rural hospitals closing. Public education gutted by vouchers. The $3 million bribe to let Ken Paxton off the hook. And Dan Patrick isn’t interested in answering for any of it.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138161455/643227305/450663877?refcode=du_em_082926_pr&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3NDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzc3OWFjMDUtZTlhMy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=UG18w9P4Kqy9eewfV-wm8a1IuUSxFG7nvs5oyKtDaKo=)

**This is the year Democrats can take Texas.**
The press is watching. The momentum is real. The GOP is scared.
_Don’t miss the moment._
For Texas,
Rep. Vikki Goodwin

name: Kailee Buller
subject: Can't afford it?
body:
I’m running to lower costs for working families.

| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter, Central New York families are doing everything right.
We're working hard, raising good kids, and trying to build a better future.
But grocery costs are steep. Energy bills are tough. Housing feels out of reach. And childcare is breaking the bank for a lot of us.
That’s not because our families are failing. It’s because Washington politicians are failing us. [**CHANGE THEM >> **](https://us.list-manage.com/mposQnGZfTl?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

Peter, I understand these struggles because I’ve lived them.
I grew up in a blue-collar family right here in Auburn. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through school, took on student debt, and became the first in my family to earn a four-year degree.
Today, I’m a working mom raising three young children, and I see firsthand how high costs are making it harder for families to get ahead.
I’M RUNNING TO CHANGE THAT.
[**MAKE THINGS AFFORDABLE AGAIN >> **](https://us.list-manage.com/1ip19l5vur7?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

Peter, in Congress, I’ll fight to:

* Lower the everyday cost of groceries, energy, housing, and child care.
* Grow good-paying jobs right here in Central New York.
* Cut wasteful spending and government red tape that drive prices higher.
* Work WITH President Trump instead of against him, to put American families FIRST!

I will always fight for the families and communities who raised me. But I can’t win this race without grassroots supporters by my side today.
Will you chip in and help us make Central New York affordable for working families again?

clean_body: I’m running to lower costs for working families. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Peter, Central New York families are doing everything right. We're working hard, raising good kids, and trying to build a better future. But grocery costs are steep. Energy bills are tough. Housing feels out of reach. And childcare is breaking the bank for a lot of us. That’s not because our families are failing. It’s because Washington politicians are failing us. Peter, I understand these struggles because I’ve lived them. I grew up in a blue-collar family right here in Auburn. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through school, took on student debt, and became the first in my family to earn a four-year degree. Today, I’m a working mom raising three young children, and I see firsthand how high costs are making it harder for families to get ahead. I’M RUNNING TO CHANGE THAT. Peter, in Congress, I’ll fight to: Lower the everyday cost of groceries, energy, housing, and child care. Grow good-paying jobs right here in Central New York. Cut wasteful spending and government red tape that drive prices higher. Work WITH President Trump instead of against him, to put American families FIRST! I will always fight for the families and communities who raised me. But I can’t win this race without grassroots supporters by my side today. Will you chip in and help us make Central New York affordable for working families again? | | | Thank you in advance. Kailee BullerCandidate for Congress | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Kailee for Congress PO Box 261 Auburn, NY 13021-0261 * USA or |

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Is this going to be a Texas that’s by and for the people?
body:
Or is this a billionaire’s world and we’re just living in it?
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
When I was a little girl growing up in Brownsville, I knew _exactly_ who Texas belonged to.
It belonged to all of us, a state where you could build a good life, raise a family, and achieve your dreams if you worked hard.
But today, under Greg Abbott, we are forced to confront a fundamental question: **Is this going to be a Texas that’s by and for the people, or is this a billionaire’s world and we’re just living in it?**
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260829_3_bworld.TPClA1&refcode=em20260829-1959&t=1&akid=1959%2E299639%2EqioGpO)**

Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

Dolly Parton was born the fourth of twelve children in a two-room cabin up in the Smoky Mountains of East Tennessee. Her daddy paid the doctor who delivered her with a sack of cornmeal. When she was a little girl, her mama stitched her winter coat out of a box of donated rags, telling her the story of Joseph and his coat of many colors while she sewed. The kids at school laughed at that coat. Dolly wore it anyway, and years later she turned that memory into one of the most beautiful songs ever written about being poor and loved at the same time. **From that cabin she rose about as high as this country allows. ** And she never once pulled the ladder up behind her. She mailed millions of books to children who needed them through her Imagination Library. She brought jobs home to the mountains that raised her. When wildfires burned out her neighbors in Gatlinburg, she quietly wrote checks to families until they could stand back up. [**Dolly exemplified everything Service Before Self means to me. name: Dylan for Wisconsin
subject: From Dylan Helmenstine - Thank You
body:
I am so, so thankful for your excitement, encouragement, and support throughout the campaign for State Treasurer.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/45b44b06f854/from-dylan-helmenstine-thank-you?e=f59034ca3e)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/_rfMAEHOEH9?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| | | | | | Hello dear friend,

I am so, so thankful for your excitement, encouragement, and support throughout the campaign for State Treasurer. I wanted to pop in now that a few weeks have passed to say thank you!
Of course, the results did not come out how I, or any of us, wanted. But, that is how it goes! I am incredibly proud of the work we put in for this race. We got folks excited about effective transparency reforms for an office that is usually quite sleepy. It is tricky to get people excited about down-ballot races, but our team got it done!
Hundreds of thousands of folks voted for our plan and vision for the office. And it was only possible with you sharing your excitement about my candidacy and with your contributions along the way. To you and “Team Dylan for Wisconsin”, thank you from the bottom of my heart.
A special shout out to my family who has always supported me along the way. It is from the big families of the O’Connell’s and the Helmenstine’s that I learned to always move forward with grace, joy, and humility. I love you all to the moon and back!
Over the past few months, I traveled all across Wisconsin. It is a _**BIG**_ state! But I had a ton of fun meeting people, learning about their communities, and seeing how much we all have in common. We posted to our socials a short round-up of the campaign. From launch day at the Helmenstine farm all the way to election night. Take a look by clicking the picture below!
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/10vMXekMad4?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| |

**Now it is time to elect****Yee Leng Xiong as Wisconsin’s next****State Treasurer!**

---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/bp7WAnJVfr_?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| | | I am so excited to support my friend Yee as he takes the reigns on the mission to flip the State Treasurer’s office! Wisconsinites deserve someone who will look out for their communities and that will ensure their money works for their families.We took this picture on Sunday, August 16th at the Madison “Forward for Wisconsin” rally. I was grateful that Yee took time during his speech to celebrate the Dylan for Wisconsin campaign. He is an all-around stellar person who will be a fantastic leader for Wisconsin. Let’s all work to get Yee across the finish line in November!
---
| |
# Click our picture above to visit Yee’s website, sign up for his email list, and contribute to his campaign!
---
| | Thank you again for all of your support for this campaign. **We truly made waves across Wisconsin**. After the hope and excitement I saw, there is no way that I am leaving public service! There’s too much work to be done. It’ll just look different for now. Follow the social media pages to stay in the know of “what is next” for me personally. You can do so by clicking the icons below.
**But right now, the most important work ahead of us is to elect David Crowley as the next governor of Wisconsin, elect the entire slate of statewide Democrats, and flip the legislature blue!**
Let’s get Wisconsin moving forward!
I’ll see you out there!Dylan Helmenstine

body:
Texas is the nation’s ultimate political testing ground for 2028.
#
Hi Peter, Maria Teresa here — co-founder of Voto Latino.
I want to talk about the moment we’re in right now, but first, [**will you make a donation to Voto Latino and support our work to register and mobilize Latinos across the nation?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20260829-2.dZnYcf&refcode=em20260829-528&t=1&akid=528%2E1366028%2EGw6cwz)
If you want to understand the future of American democracy, stop looking at Washington D.C. — **look at Texas. The nation’s ultimate political testing ground for 2028.**
What happens here today will inevitably shape what happens across America.
