Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. | | | I’ll be straight with you. Our fundraising has slowed down, and we’re behind where we planned to be at this point in the month. That may sound like a line from a campaign email, but the consequences are real. A smaller budget means fewer doors knocked, fewer voters reached, and fewer resources to respond when national Republicans launch their next round of attacks. I represent a district where elections are decided on a knife’s edge. There is no safe corner of Southwest Washington we can afford to ignore—and no substitute for showing up and earning people’s trust. That’s how I’ve always approached this job. I don’t vote based on what will earn me applause in Washington, D.C. I listen to the people who sent me there: loggers, tradespeople, small-business owners, parents trying to afford groceries, and families wondering whether they’ll ever be able to buy a home. Sometimes that means standing up to Republicans. Sometimes it means standing up to my own party. Every time, it means putting this district first. That independence is exactly why national Republicans want me gone. They can’t dismiss me as another party-line politician, so they’ll spend millions trying to distort my record and define me before I can reach voters myself. We need the resources to answer them—and to keep talking with people in every community, not only the places political consultants consider convenient. I’m not asking you to solve our entire budget shortfall. That isn’t how this campaign has ever worked. We win when thousands of people each take responsibility for a small piece of the work. [**Will you contribute $10, $25, or whatever makes sense for you today to help us close this gap and keep our voter outreach fully funded?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138165586/643235996/-995582223?refcode=260829-slowed&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyNmY0YzYzZC1mOWEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=tl9zHO08cSTtXx6ERKYVYhYU3bSrbH2K8xr_RfbRzQo=)

Joe Walsh has known Mike Rogers for years. He served with him in Congress. On this week's Tequila Talk, he said something about Rogers that you will not hear from anyone who did not sit in that building with him.
And that was not even the part of the conversation that will get us yelled at.
Cliff said, plainly and for the record, that he believes Abdul El-Sayed--the Democrat running for Senate in Michigan--is an antisemite, and explained exactly what brought him to that conclusion. Joe, who is not a Democrat and has spent the last decade telling his old party what it has become, agreed on the principle: bigotry disqualifies a candidate, and it does not matter which flavor of bigotry it is or which team benefits.
Then they said the thing that will get the replies going. Neither of them would vote in that race. Not for El-Sayed. Not for Rogers.

**Join the National Workers Strike Back meeting**[**TOMORROW, Sunday, Aug 30th at 12pm PT / 3pm ET.**](https://us.list-manage.com/V69NFJkGLsy?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)

**We’ll discuss the important lessons of our independent socialist Congressional campaign, and next steps to continue advancing the struggle of the international working class against capitalism and its endless wars.**

[**Become a member of Workers Strike Back**](https://us.list-manage.com/wC8G3QqsKul?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)**today and help us prepare for the next fight forward!**

---

---
| | Dear Peter,
Kshama and our team are encouraging everyone who supported this historic campaign to join Kshama's organization, Workers Strike Back, and to attend tomorrow’s online meeting. This will be the strongest way to carry forward our momentum and continue building movements to confront the Democratic and Republican parties, both of which represent the war-profiteering billionaires and multimillionaires.
We got the highest ever vote for an open Marxist Congressional candidate, winning 17.3 percent. Workers Strike Back is hosting an online meeting on Sunday August 30th at 12pm PT/3pm ET to draw out the important lessons from our campaign, and to discuss next steps to fight the rich and their political servants.
If you haven’t yet, please check out our [end of campaign statement](https://us.list-manage.com/MNnjmp3tuJn?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15), which is copied below:
_Our campaign was by far the strongest ever by an openly Marxist candidate for the U.S. Congress._
_We've won a historic 17.3 percent of the vote in a five-way race, in Washington’s sprawling Ninth Congressional District. Over 24,500 people voted for a Marxist in the district, which spans suburban areas with a significant proportion of Republican voters in addition to large parts of the major urban areas of Seattle and Bellevue._
_This is an incredible result! We need to use this to continue building movements that confront the Democratic and Republican parties, both of which represent the war-profiteering billionaires and multimillionaires._
_We ran on electrifying demands like free healthcare for all funded by taxing the rich, ending all military aid to Israel and a permanent arms embargo on Israel, and national rent control. All of these are extremely popular among the working class in this district and nationally._
_We achieved this result despite the many obstacles we faced._
_Both the Republican and Democratic parties maneuvered by running candidates specifically to block our campaign from getting into the November election, which would have resulted in a head-to-head battle between our campaign and genocidal Democrat Adam Smith._
_We faced a corporate media blackout and hostility and outright attacks from DSA leaders and many "progressive" podcasters._
_Many labor leaders shamelessly endorsed Adam Smith, while others remained silent, effectively supporting Smith._
_All of these obstacles were predictable. Our decade on the Seattle City Council showed what a threat we are to the political establishment and those who give them cover. We used our decade on the Seattle City Council to relentlessly build working-class movements, winning four elections and unparalleled victories such as the nation's highest minimum wage, which also led to substantive raises for tens of millions of workers across the United States, defeating Jeff Bezos to win the Amazon Tax, and repeatedly beating corporate landlords to win unprecedented renters' rights._
_Despite not making it into the November election, we've provided a powerful example of what's possible by running an openly Marxist independent campaign based on class struggle rather than making peace with the political establishment or its legions of gatekeepers._
_The DSA strategy of appeasing and, worse, rehabilitating the discredited Democratic leadership and their rotten party is a dead end. In this age of imperialist war and climate catastrophe, we simply have no time to fuck around._
_We urgently need militant movements of the working class and a new mass party that can defeat the billionaires and both their parties. And we need revolutionary socialist campaigns like mine that don’t try to join the establishment and help administer the capitalist system, but are fighting to overthrow it._
Solidarity,
Kshama for Congress

subject: The reality of having an August primary election.

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3048%2E251025%2ETfR9ML ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3048%2E251025%2ETfR9ML ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter, I
have to be honest with you.

The reality of having an August primary election date is not great. It’s
pretty terrible timing for a campaign powered 100% by people like you.

Let me explain.

For the past few months, we’ve been running ads, making tight budget
decisions, and relying on members of our grassroots team to power us through the
final stretch of the primary campaign.

We were facing $70 million in outside spending against us. We couldn’t
afford to play it safe. So, to put it bluntly, we practically drained our
bank account leading up to August 4th.

We made it through the primary, but that’s only half the battle.

The general election is here, and Mike Rogers has $51 million backing him
to blanket the airwaves with misleading attack ads.

It sounds daunting, but I’ve counted on this team before, and you’ve never
let me down. I’m hoping I can count on you again today,
Peter. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260829-3-ak.ztlF8S&amount=10&refcode=em20260829-3048&t=1004&akid=3048%2E251025%2ETfR9ML ]Please, pitch in
$10 or any amount to help us get back on our feet as quickly
as possible so that we can reach undecided voters before Rogers does.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260829-3-ak.ztlF8S&amount=10&refcode=em20260829-3048&t=1023&akid=3048%2E251025%2ETfR9ML ]Donate $10 ››

In solidarity,

Abdul

Anatomy of an Attempted Takedown
| | August 29, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/7qh7h8h9n965xlszh6/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvcDl1ZWg5aDJwbW5xMmhtNmdndzZrYXBteHF3NzBzcmhyNDgwZQ==) | |
---
| Hi Friend — No one has even seen the film yet. But the attacks have already started. We are preparing to release[**TRAPPED (Detroit)**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/z2hghnhelekxmvaph0/dHJhcHBlZC52b3Rl) — a documentary built around real people, real records, and questions that deserve answers. Yet we are already being flooded with comments like the one below—people calling our work a “conspiracy,” warning others not to believe it, and linking to a recent story from the publication WIRED as supposed proof. |
---
Again, outside of our production team, **no one has seen the documentary.**
In case you've never heard of WIRED it is a Condé Nast technology and culture publication that has increasingly moved into political reporting, where it has taken a distinctly progressive and consistently adversarial posture toward President Trump and his administration.
They've written negative articles about us for years, just like hundreds of other outlets. Until now our general rule has been to just ignore them.
We're not going to do that anymore.
Instead, we’re going to show you the anatomy of these attempted takedowns—how a conclusion is chosen, how the facts are arranged around it, which answers are ignored, and how insinuation is made to look like reporting. Once you see the pattern, it becomes much easier to recognize. And in an age of relentless information warfare, the ability to see through the hype and think for yourself has never been more important.
Their most recent reporting describes us as the group “responsible for” the “debunked” _2000 Mules._
So, a little history matters.
First, True the Vote did not make _2000 Mules_. I believe the film was enormously helpful in waking millions of Americans up to serious vulnerabilities in our elections. But it was not our film, and it is simply inaccurate to describe True the Vote as the group “responsible for” it.
Our work began long before the film. In late 2020, after speaking with several confidential sources, we began purchasing and analyzing geospatial data in and around ballot drop boxes and nonprofit organizations. We identified patterns we believed warranted further investigation and took our findings to law enforcement, including the FBI and the Georgia Bureau of Investigation. That was more than a year before anyone discussed using the work in a movie.
When the Washington Post later asked Dinesh D’Souza how much editorial control True the Vote had over _2000 Mules_ , his answer was simple: **“Zero.”**
We stand behind the work we provided. But we did not write the script, choose the cuts, shape the narrative, or control the presentation.
Our position was always that geospatial data was sufficient evidence to support probable cause — a lead that law enforcement to follow to de-anonymize devices, interview people, subpoena records, and investigate. We couldn’t do those things. Authorities could.
We secured data from the same sources used by authorities. We had analysts in common, so there could be no question as to credibility.
But something extraordinary happened as politicos became aware of our project: **The discussions we were having about investigations into our data stopped.**
To our knowledge, every investigative effort involving the data we had provided came to a halt. The evidence wasn’t followed through to its logical conclusion. The devices weren’t de-anonymized. The people behind the patterns weren’t investigated. And the media dutifully began to spread the talking points that we had been "debunked".
There is now sworn testimony raising serious questions about why.
In previously sealed Fulton County grand-jury testimony, former U.S. Senator David Perdue testified that then-GBI Director Vic Reynolds had reviewed evidence involving cell-phone data, video, testimony and bank records and considered it compelling enough to investigate. Perdue further testified that Reynolds later told him:
**“I’m a team player. If the governor doesn’t want to investigate, we’re not going to investigate.”**
Read the grand-jury[ **transcript archive**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/7qh7h8h9n965xetzh6/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubGF3ZmFyZW1lZGlhLm9yZy9wcm9qZWN0cy1zZXJpZXMvdGVzdGltb255LWhlYXJkLWJ5LXRoZS10cnVtcC1ncmFuZC1qdXJ5LWluLWZ1bHRvbi1jb3VudHk=)**:**
[](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/7qh7h8h9n965xetzh6/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubGF3ZmFyZW1lZGlhLm9yZy9wcm9qZWN0cy1zZXJpZXMvdGVzdGltb255LWhlYXJkLWJ5LXRoZS10cnVtcC1ncmFuZC1qdXJ5LWluLWZ1bHRvbi1jb3VudHk=)
---
Read the report on Perdue’s [**testimony**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/p8heh9h4q42oe3iqh3/aHR0cHM6Ly9iYWRsYW5kcy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vcC9ncmFuZC1qdXJ5LXRlc3RpbW9ueS1mcm9tLXNlbmF0b3I=):
[](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/p8heh9h4q42oe3iqh3/aHR0cHM6Ly9iYWRsYW5kcy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vcC9ncmFuZC1qdXJ5LXRlc3RpbW9ueS1mcm9tLXNlbmF0b3I=)
---
### **WIRED Trusts Geospatial Data—Until True the Vote Uses It**
Now consider this. WIRED has repeatedly reported on the accuracy of geospatial evidence.
When WIRED investigated visitors to Jeffrey Epstein’s island using commercially brokered location data from the advertising ecosystem, WIRED said the coordinates could pinpoint locations **“within a few centimeters.”** They used that data to trace movements, routes, homes and workplaces.
Read WIRED’s Epstein geolocation [**investigation**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/kkhmh6hnxn5vp2ulh7/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2lyZWQuY29tL3N0b3J5L2plZmZyZXktZXBzdGVpbi1pc2xhbmQtdmlzaXRvcnMtZGF0YS1icm9rZXItbGVhay8=):
[](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/kkhmh6hnxn5vp2ulh7/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2lyZWQuY29tL3N0b3J5L2plZmZyZXktZXBzdGVpbi1pc2xhbmQtdmlzaXRvcnMtZGF0YS1icm9rZXItbGVhay8=)
---
When the FBI used geofence data after January 6, WIRED described location technology capable of placing phones **“within a few yards.”**
Read WIRED’s January 6 [**investigation**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/25h2hoh3m38wxof3h4/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2lyZWQuY29tL3N0b3J5L2NhcGl0b2wtcmlvdC1nb29nbGUtZ2VvZmVuY2Utd2FycmFudC8=):
[](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/25h2hoh3m38wxof3h4/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2lyZWQuY29tL3N0b3J5L2NhcGl0b2wtcmlvdC1nb29nbGUtZ2VvZmVuY2Utd2FycmFudC8=)
---
Different datasets have different capabilities, to be sure, but WIRED clearly understands that geospatial information can be powerful investigative evidence. So, why disparage ours? Because our evidence didn't serve their narrative.
And the catcalls that we'd been "debunked" were erroneously echoed all over the country.
_Investigate the evidence. That was all we asked for._
Instead, the investigations stopped, _2000 Mules_ became the target, and now that same label is being used to tell people what to think about **TRAPPED (Detroit)** before they have even seen it.
### **And While We Were Preparing This Very Email ... WIRED Strikes Again**
Incredibly, while we were preparing this response, **WIRED published another hit piece on us.**[**Here it is**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/3ohphkh3p32g84arhn/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2lyZWQuY29tL3N0b3J5L3dhZmZsZS1ob3VzZS10ZWxlcG9ydGVyLWdyZWdnLXBoaWxsaXBzLWlzLXN0aWxsLW9uLXRoZS10cnVtcC1hZG1pbmlzdHJhdGlvbnMtcGF5cm9sbC8=) — written **AFTER** I'd talked with the reporter, David Gilbert.
This time the headline itself calls Gregg Phillips the “Waffle House Teleporter” — taking one of the most vulnerable moments of a man’s documented battle with metastatic cancer and turning it into clickbait — even after he knew the full story, because I'd shared it with him.
Disgusting.
Then the story piles on.
WIRED says Gregg had “no past experience working in emergency response.” That is not true.
Gregg spent decades working on the ground in disaster zones through nonprofit and faith-based efforts, including work surrounding Katrina and Haiti. [**Even WIRED’s own coverage**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/3ohphkh3p32g84arhn/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2lyZWQuY29tL3N0b3J5L3dhZmZsZS1ob3VzZS10ZWxlcG9ydGVyLWdyZWdnLXBoaWxsaXBzLWlzLXN0aWxsLW9uLXRoZS10cnVtcC1hZG1pbmlzdHJhdGlvbnMtcGF5cm9sbC8=)quotes FEMA praising Gregg’s ‘service, dedication, and leadership’ and saying he played a _‘pivotal role’_ in stabilizing the Office of Response and Recovery and advancing reforms.
Then WIRED reaches backward to suggest there is some mystery about Gregg’s relationship with True the Vote because he once served on our board. There is no mystery.
Gregg served on True the Vote’s board from 2014 through 2017. He later assisted us as a contractor on research from 2020–2023. He is not currently a board member, employee, or member of the True the Vote team.
We think Gregg is great. He supports our work. He has appeared on my podcast. I have spoken publicly about his battle against cancer. But he has not _“come back to work with True the Vote.”_
WIRED also resurrects years-old financial allegations wholly unrelated to Gregg’s current government status or TRAPPED.
I am writing a full response to address those separately and will post on our website. It's all nonsense, but because we seem to again be in the eye of the storm, and I'm sick of it, we're going to address every allegation.
Even then, mark my words: it will never be enough. Their goal is not honest reporting. No answer I give, no documentation I provide, and no factual error I correct will ever change the story they have already decided to tell.
**And that certainty is especially striking coming from WIRED reporter David Gilbert.** Living thousands of miles away in Ireland, he repeatedly tells Americans what to think about local election disputes, while the citizens actually living through them struggle to get their evidence heard.
WIRED — and their cohorts — have been doing this for years: decide the conclusion, attach the label, and discredit the evidence before readers ever get a fair chance to consider it. That is not reporting. It is narrative enforcement.
President Trump calls it “fake news.” Whatever label you prefer, the pattern is impossible to miss.
I hoped for better from WIRED. I really did. My hopes were misplaced.
### **A Word About Ramon Jackson**
And while we are correcting the record, a word about **Ramon Jackson**.
Ramon is one of the Detroit citizens whose firsthand experiences, affidavits, and years-long legal fight are part of the story documented in **TRAPPED (Detroit)**. WIRED invokes the dismissal of his lawsuit as a reason readers should doubt the documentary, so it is important to understand what actually happened.
WIRED tells readers that Ramon’s lawsuit was dismissed, but leaves out an important distinction:
**His case was dismissed at the pleading stage.** There was no trial. There was no evidentiary hearing. And there was no judicial finding that the experiences Ramon and other Detroit citizens documented were false.
Ramon had no army of lawyers. He filed pro se, kept fighting through the Sixth Circuit, and ultimately carried his case to the U.S. Supreme Court.
For years Ramon has been trying to get someone to actually hear the evidence.
No one has.
**Justice delayed is justice denied.**
That is one reason TRAPPED (Detroit) matters.
TRAPPED (Detroit) is not a movie built around a political narrative. It is a documentary investigation.
It centers on Detroit citizens, public records, sworn statements, litigation, government documents, and questions that have been buried or ignored for years.
And if we're already being flooded with attacks before the public has even seen the evidence, that should tell you something.
### **Don't let anyone do your thinking for you.**
For years, we have absorbed labels, smears, and shorthand characterizations while continuing to do the work.
We have had enough. It's time to fight back.
[**TRAPPED (Detroit)**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/z2hghnhelekxmvaph0/dHJhcHBlZC52b3Rl)is over the target and the Call to Action, to check your own record using [**Scan. Check. Protect,** ](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/r8u4m7xrd8toh3o4g63c2hdxq0g54b7hxorp2/l2hehmhlxln7pms6h0/c2NhbmNoZWNrcHJvdGVjdC5vcmc=)is one of the few remaining ways to improve election integrity before the midterms. Please help spread the word. Do not wait on government to act. Do what you can, now.
Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW!
Ever onward —
---
**P.S. — Olive branch withdrawn, WIRED.**
I had planned to end this letter by saying something positive about WIRED. I reached out to them in good faith and we'd had several conversations. And yet they still chose to publish another hit piece, resurfacing years of fake news about us and citing it as fact, then piling on with fake news of their own.
Here is what really bothers me about this story, this time.
I answered David Gilbert’s questions. WIRED used part of my response — and then told its readers I “did not respond” to the question about Gregg’s former role on our board.
That is not true. I did respond. I specifically explained that Gregg joined the board in 2014 and rolled off in early 2017. I also explained the IRS filing issue: a former CPA failed to remove Gregg’s name from a later return, our accounting was subsequently moved to new CPAs and auditors, and corrected filings were made. I even explained that the IRS website itself currently shows multiple filings and broken links, including 404 errors that appear to involve amended returns, none of which do we have any control over.
You may not like my answer. You may decide not to use it. But you cannot tell your readers I failed to respond when I did.
So — my outreach got us a headline mocking Gregg, recycled false allegations from years ago, a misleading account of Gregg's FEMA experience, an errant implication about his relationship with True the Vote, and yet another judgment about a documentary the reporter has never seen. There is no value in any of this other than to needlessly foment more anger.
**This is exactly why we stopped talking to reporters.**
And so, to WIRED, because I know you will read this, consider this P.S. a direct request to correct the record.
You state that Gregg had “no past experience working in emergency response.” That is false as written. Gregg has spent decades responding to disasters and leading relief efforts through nonprofit and faith-based work. If what you mean is that he lacked previous federal emergency-management experience, say that.
You state that I did not respond when asked about Gregg’s former board role. I did respond**before publication** and provided both the board timeline and an explanation of the IRS filings. Correct that statement.
You state as fact that TRAPPED (Detroit) “makes allegations about widespread and systemic voter fraud,” despite the fact that you have not seen the documentary. If you have not reviewed the film, you cannot truthfully tell your readers what it alleges. Retract or substantiate that statement.
And in your earlier coverage, you told readers that Ramon Jackson’s lawsuit was dismissed for “failure to produce sufficient evidence.” His case was dismissed at the pleading stage. There was no trial and no evidentiary hearing adjudicating the truth of the evidence he brought forward. You should correct that characterization as well. This is not the first time you've been notified.
I genuinely hoped we could find common ground around something much bigger than any of us: the profound risks artificial intelligence now poses to America’s technically vulnerable election infrastructure. That's why I reached out to know. You know that.
The blessing and curse of AI has arrived at the doorstep of thousands of local election offices — many with little or no dedicated IT staff. We have to start talking seriously about what that means.
Maybe someday we can talk about it with WIRED, but not today and not for the foreseeable future. For now, I’m done talking to — or about you.
Oh, except for the pending litigation against you. **I now look forward to that conversation.**

WIRED invokes the dismissal of his lawsuit as a reason readers should doubt the documentary, so it is important to understand what actually happened. WIRED tells readers that Ramon’s lawsuit was dismissed, but leaves out an important distinction: His case was dismissed at the pleading stage. There was no trial. There was no evidentiary hearing. And there was no judicial finding that the experiences Ramon and other Detroit citizens documented were false. Ramon had no army of lawyers. He filed pro se, kept fighting through the Sixth Circuit, and ultimately carried his case to the U.S. Supreme Court. For years Ramon has been trying to get someone to actually hear the evidence. No one has. Justice delayed is justice denied. That is one reason TRAPPED (Detroit) matters. TRAPPED (Detroit) is not a movie built around a political narrative. It is a documentary investigation. It centers on Detroit citizens, public records, sworn statements, litigation, government documents, and questions that have been buried or ignored for years. And if we're already being flooded with attacks before the public has even seen the evidence, that should tell you something. Don't let anyone do your thinking for you. For years, we have absorbed labels, smears, and shorthand characterizations while continuing to do the work. We have had enough. It's time to fight back. over the target and the Call to Action, to check your own record using one of the few remaining ways to improve election integrity before the midterms. Please help spread the word. Do not wait on government to act. Do what you can, now. Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW! Ever onward — P.S. — Olive branch withdrawn, WIRED. I had planned to end this letter by saying something positive about WIRED. I reached out to them in good faith and we'd had several conversations. And yet they still chose to publish another hit piece, resurfacing years of fake news about us and citing it as fact, then piling on with fake news of their own. Here is what really bothers me about this story, this time. I answered David Gilbert’s questions. WIRED used part of my response — and then told its readers I “did not respond” to the question about Gregg’s former role on our board. That is not true. I did respond. I specifically explained that Gregg joined the board in 2014 and rolled off in early 2017. I also explained the IRS filing issue: a former CPA failed to remove Gregg’s name from a later return, our accounting was subsequently moved to new CPAs and auditors, and corrected filings were made. I even explained that the IRS website itself currently shows multiple filings and broken links, including 404 errors that appear to involve amended returns, none of which do we have any control over. You may not like my answer. You may decide not to use it. But you cannot tell your readers I failed to respond when I did. So — my outreach got us a headline mocking Gregg, recycled false allegations from years ago, a misleading account of Gregg's FEMA experience, an errant implication about his relationship with True the Vote, and yet another judgment about a documentary the reporter has never seen. There is no value in any of this other than to needlessly foment more anger. This is exactly why we stopped talking to reporters. And so, to WIRED, because I know you will read this, consider this P.S. a direct request to correct the record. You state that Gregg had “no past experience working in emergency response.” That is false as written. Gregg has spent decades responding to disasters and leading relief efforts through nonprofit and faith-based work. If what you mean is that he lacked previous federal emergency-management experience, say that. You state that I did not respond when asked about Gregg’s former board role. I did respondbefore publication and provided both the board timeline and an explanation of the IRS filings. Correct that statement. You state as fact that TRAPPED (Detroit) “makes allegations about widespread and systemic voter fraud,” despite the fact that you have not seen the documentary. If you have not reviewed the film, you cannot truthfully tell your readers what it alleges. Retract or substantiate that statement. And in your earlier coverage, you told readers that Ramon Jackson’s lawsuit was dismissed for “failure to produce sufficient evidence.” His case was dismissed at the pleading stage. There was no trial and no evidentiary hearing adjudicating the truth of the evidence he brought forward. You should correct that characterization as well. This is not the first time you've been notified. I genuinely hoped we could find common ground around something much bigger than any of us: the profound risks artificial intelligence now poses to America’s technically vulnerable election infrastructure. That's why I reached out to know. You know that. The blessing and curse of AI has arrived at the doorstep of thousands of local election offices — many with little or no dedicated IT staff. We have to start talking seriously about what that means. Maybe someday we can talk about it with WIRED, but not today and not for the foreseeable future. For now, I’m done talking to — or about you. Oh, except for the pending litigation against you. I now look forward to that conversation. | | == Update your or unsubscribe © 2026 True the Vote 3120 Southwest Frwy Ste 101, PMB 19128, Houston, Texas 77098-4520

| | | I just got back from Ukraine.
I’m one of a small handful of Members of Congress to travel there in the past year — and I need to tell you what I saw, and why it matters so much to this fight.
For over four years, Ukraine has been fighting for its survival against Vladimir Putin's unprovoked invasion. I've stood with them since day one. I've led bipartisan legislation to arm Ukraine's military. I've fought to hold Russia accountable for war crimes. I've warned, again and again, that appeasing Putin doesn't bring peace — it invites the next invasion.
**Here's what I saw on this trip: A country still fighting, still resilient, still holding the line — and increasingly uncertain about whether America is still standing 100% behind them.**
That uncertainty didn't come from nowhere. Donald Trump has spent his presidency squeezing Ukraine while handing Vladimir Putin exactly what he wants. **I didn't take this trip for a photo opportunity. I took it because Ukraine needs to know that not every American leader has abandoned them — and because I wanted to see, firsthand, what's actually at stake in Ukraine.**
This is exactly why Equal Opportunity Now exists. We need Democrats in office who understand that standing up to authoritarian aggression isn't optional — it's central to who we are as a country. MAGA Republicans cannot be trusted with this. Time and again, they have shown they'll trade away our allies' security for a photo op with a dictator.

clean_body: | | | | = | | | I just got back from Ukraine. I’m one of a small handful of Members of Congress to travel there in the past year — and I need to tell you what I saw, and why it matters so much to this fight. For over four years, Ukraine has been fighting for its survival against Vladimir Putin's unprovoked invasion. I've stood with them since day one. I've led bipartisan legislation to arm Ukraine's military. I've fought to hold Russia accountable for war crimes. I've warned, again and again, that appeasing Putin doesn't bring peace — it invites the next invasion. Here's what I saw on this trip: A country still fighting, still resilient, still holding the line — and increasingly uncertain about whether America is still standing 100% behind them. That uncertainty didn't come from nowhere. Donald Trump has spent his presidency squeezing Ukraine while handing Vladimir Putin exactly what he wants. I didn't take this trip for a photo opportunity. I took it because Ukraine needs to know that not every American leader has abandoned them — and because I wanted to see, firsthand, what's actually at stake in Ukraine. This is exactly why Equal Opportunity Now exists. We need Democrats in office who understand that standing up to authoritarian aggression isn't optional — it's central to who we are as a country. MAGA Republicans cannot be trusted with this. Time and again, they have shown they'll trade away our allies' security for a photo op with a dictator. = = | | | = Ukraine is still fighting. America still needs to stand with them. — Raja Krishnamoorthi Founder | Equal Opportunity Now | = Equal Opportunity Now is d/b/a Reviving American Jobs Again PAC (RAJA PAC) Equal Opportunity Now P.O.
